He has played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and the [[Chinese Basketball Association]]. Telfair was picked thirteenth overall in the [[2004 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] on the heels of an eminent high school career playing for [[Abraham Lincoln High School (Brooklyn)|Abraham Lincoln High]]. He had committed to the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|University of Louisville]] during his senior year, but decided to turn professional instead.{{cite web | last=Hodge | first=Bill | title=Hodge: Telfair adds his name to NBA draft | website=ESPN.com | date=2004-05-05 | url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/news/story?id=1795416 | access-date=2025-05-04}}{{cite web |url=http://louisville.scout.com/2/249615.html |title=Pitino says Telfair will not play at Louisville |publisher=Scout.com (Louisville "edition") |date=April 6, 2004 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060522220333/http://louisville.scout.com/2/249615.html |archive-date=May 22, 2006 }} Telfair is a cousin of former NBA player [[Stephon Marbury]].{{cite web|title=Sebastian Telfair draft bio|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2005/index|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170224140245/http://www.espn.com/nba/draft2005/index|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 24, 2017}} ==Early years== Telfair was born in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York (state)|New York]], the son of Erica Telfair and Otis Telfair, a [[Vietnam War]] veteran who served as a [[United States Marine Corps|Marine]].Ian O'Connor, ''The Jump: Sebastian Telfair and the High Stakes Business of High School Ball.'' [Emmaus, Pa.]: Rodale, 2005. p. 7-16 Living in the Surfside Gardens projects in Brooklyn, he attended [[Abraham Lincoln High School (Brooklyn)|Abraham Lincoln High School]], where he became one of the most highly lauded and coveted high school basketball prospects in the country.Ian O'Connor, ''The Jump: Sebastian Telfair and the High Stakes Business of High School Ball.'' [Emmaus, Pa.]: Rodale, 2005. p. 2-3 Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Telfair was listed as the No. 2 point guard and No. 6 player in the nation in 2004.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Sebastian-Telfair-4018;_ylt=AmwU9DX.fYkAboSoXPk2GRJGPZB4 Sebastian Telfair Recruiting Profile] Originally, he had committed to the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|University of Louisville]] and head coach [[Rick Pitino]]. However, he later had a change of mind and went pro instead, a decision precipitated by a fatal shooting that occurred at the apartment complex where his family lived. ==Professional career== === Portland Trail Blazers (2004–2006) === Telfair was selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] with the thirteenth overall pick in the [[2004 NBA draft]]. On January 1, 2005, Telfair scored 14 points on five-for-eleven shooting, making four of five [[free throw]]s to go with five rebounds and five assists with one turnover.{{Cite web |title=Warriors vs Trail Blazers, January 1, 2005 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200501010POR.html |access-date=2025-05-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} In February 2005, interim coach [[Kevin Pritchard]] promoted Telfair to the team's starting lineup. Telfair notched 6.8 points and 3.3 assists per contest. The Blazers ultimately lost 23 of their final 28 games that season, finishing with the team's worst record since [[1973–74 Portland Trail Blazers season|1973–74]]. Under new head coach [[Nate McMillan]], Telfair began the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]] as the starting point guard and was occasionally paired in the backcourt with another high school draftee taken in 2005, [[Martell Webster]]. Telfair improved upon his [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05]] numbers; though his production was still seen {{By whom|date=February 2010}} by multiple commentators as being somewhat below par for an NBA starting point guard. As a result, Telfair experienced increasing pressure from various local media. In December 2005, Telfair suffered a thumb injury and was replaced in the starting lineup by [[Steve Blake]], who went on to have fewer turnovers and more assists. Telfair returned to the court on January 9, 2006, after having missed twelve games. Blake continued as the starting point guard with Telfair coming off the bench. Although the Trail Blazers had already been eliminated from [[2006 NBA playoffs|playoff]] contention that season, Telfair scored the game-winning basket against the [[Houston Rockets]] on April 5, 2006. === Boston Celtics (2006–2007) === On June 28, 2006, the Trail Blazers traded Telfair, along with center [[Theo Ratliff]] and a 2008 second-round pick, to the [[Boston Celtics]] for guard [[Dan Dickau]], center–forward [[Raef LaFrentz]], and the 7th overall pick in the [[2006 NBA draft]], [[Randy Foye]], who was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for the 6th overall pick, [[Brandon Roy]]. Telfair wore number 30, as his traditional number 31 was retired by the Celtics. On April 24, 2007, Celtics managing partner [[Wyc Grousbeck]] announced that Telfair's [[nameplate]] on his Celtics locker had been removed and did not expect him back for the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2847755 Celtics move toward severing ties with Telfair], ESPN.com news services, published April 25, 2007[https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2007/04/25/supersonics-fire-coach-bob-hill/ SuperSonics fire coach Bob Hill – Orlando Sentinel] === Minnesota Timberwolves (2007–2009) === On July 31, 2007, the Celtics traded Telfair, along with [[Al Jefferson]], [[Gerald Green]], [[Ryan Gomes]], [[Theo Ratliff]] and two first-round draft picks, to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for [[Kevin Garnett]].{{cite news |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=ap-celtics-garnett |title=Celtics land Garnett in unprecedented 7-for-1 deal |agency=Associated Press |date=July 31, 2007 |first=Howard |last=Ulman |access-date=July 31, 2007 }} He was given the # 3 jersey while with Minnesota, the same number that his cousin, [[Stephon Marbury]] wore while playing for that team. In the 2007–08 season, Telfair had his best season as a pro, averaging 9.3 points and 5.9 assists per game. Telfair also had a stretch of five games in which he had 40 assists and only four turnovers. He wore number 3 for the Timberwolves because the number 31 had been taken by shooting guard [[Ricky Davis]]. On July 22, 2008, the Minnesota Timberwolves re-signed Telfair to a three-year contract. Because the Timberwolves fired head coach [[Randy Wittman]] and replaced him with interim coach [[Kevin McHale (basketball)|Kevin McHale]], Telfair played for his sixth coach on his third NBA team in his fifth NBA season. He played in 75 games including 43 starts. === Los Angeles Clippers (2009–2010) === On July 20, 2009, Telfair was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] along with [[Craig Smith (basketball, born 1983)|Craig Smith]] and [[Mark Madsen (basketball)|Mark Madsen]] in exchange for [[Quentin Richardson]].{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews090720.html | title=Clippers Acquire Telfair, Smith and Madsen from Minnesota for Richardson | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=July 20, 2009 | access-date=July 21, 2009}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2010)=== On February 17, 2010, Telfair was traded from the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] as part of a three-team, six-player trade that sent [[Antawn Jamison]] from the [[Washington Wizards]] to Cleveland, [[Zydrunas Ilgauskas]], a [[2010 NBA draft|2010 first-round pick]] (which became [[Lazar Hayward]]) and the rights to [[Emir Preldžić]] from Cleveland to Washington, [[Drew Gooden (basketball)|Drew Gooden]] from Washington to Los Angeles, and [[Al Thornton]] from Los Angeles to Washington.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/trade_100217.html|title=Wizards Acquire Ilgauskas, Thornton and First-Round Pick In Three-Team Deal|work=NBA.com|date=February 17, 2010|access-date=February 17, 2010}} === Return to Minnesota (2010–2011) === On July 26, 2010, Telfair was traded back to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], along with [[Delonte West]], for [[Ramon Sessions]] and [[Ryan Hollins]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5412223|title=Wolves Trade Sessions to Cavaliers|work = ESPN.com|date=July 26, 2010|access-date=July 26, 2010}} === Phoenix Suns (2011–2013) === Right after the [[2011 NBA lockout]] ended, Telfair signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]] on December 9, 2011.[https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7336553/phoenix-suns-waive-vince-carter-sign-guards-sebastian-telfair-shannon-brown Phoenix Suns waive Vince Carter, sign guards Sebastian Telfair, Shannon Brown - ESPN] His contract had him initially staying for one year, but he received a team option to play for a second season in Phoenix. Telfair started for the Suns in a 91–87 victory against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. Telfair would score a season high 21 points in a 105–91 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. During the month of April in the shortened season, Telfair averaged an impressive 10.9 points and 3.6 assists on a .522 shooting percentage. In other months, he had averaged 4.7 points and 1.9 assists on a .358 shooting percentage.[http://valleyofthesuns.com/2012/05/17/sebastian-telfair-build-stellar-final-month/ Sebastian Telfair preparing to build on stellar final month] ===Toronto Raptors (2013)=== On February 21, 2013, Telfair was traded to the Toronto Raptors in exchange for [[Hamed Haddadi]] and a second-round draft pick.{{Cite web |url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/raptors-acquire-telfair-from-suns-for-haddadi-pick/ |title=Raptors Acquire Telfair From Suns For Haddadi, Pick |access-date=February 22, }} He became a free agent in the summer of 2013. === Tianjin Ronggang (2013–2014) === In October 2013, Telfair signed a one-year deal with the [[Tianjin Gold Lions|Tianjin Ronggang]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/106981/sebastian-telfair-signs-in-china-with-tianjin.html Sebastian Telfair signs in China with Tianjin] ===Oklahoma City Thunder Thunder that same day.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_telfair_141126|title=Thunder Waives Sebastian Telfair|date=November 26, 2014|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 26, 2014}} === Xinjiang Flying Tigers (2014–2015) === On December 2, 2014, Telfair signed with the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]] for the rest of the 2014–15 CBA season.{{Cite web |url=http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/sebastian-telfair-heads-xinjiang/ |title=Sebastian Telfair heads to Xinjiang |access-date=December 28, 2014 |archive-date=December 28, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141228131154/http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/sebastian-telfair-heads-xinjiang/ |url-status=dead }} === Fuijan Sturgeons (2016–2017) === On November 18, 2016, Telfair signed with the [[Fujian Sturgeons|Fuijan Sturgeons]].{{Cite web|title=Former NBA Journeyman Sebastian Telfair Set to Play in China|url=https://www.chinatopix.com/articles/106431/20161118/nba-sebastian-telfair-china.htm|access-date=January 19, 2022|website=China Topix}} ==Legal issues== {{Cleanup section|date=February 2025|reason=the legal issues section needs copyediting and does not use wikivoice.}} On October 16, 2006, Telfair had a chain, valued at $50,000, snatched from his possession outside [[Sean Combs|Sean "Diddy" Combs]]'s restaurant, Justin's. As it happened, rapper [[Fabolous]] was shot outside the same club shortly afterward.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2632410 |title=Police investigating Telfair in connection with shooting |work=[[ESPN.com]] |access-date=October 19, 2006 |date=October 19, 2006 }} The following night, Telfair left a pre-season basketball game against the [[New York Knicks]] at [[Madison Square Garden]] to observe a police lineup, but he did not identify any of the potential suspects.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2630170 |title=Telfair fails to spot chain-ripping thief in police lineup |work=[[ESPN.com]] |access-date=October 18, 2006 |date=October 18, 2006 }} Telfair and a friend, Al Eden Fuentes,{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2844534 |title=Celtics guard Telfair arrested in NY on gun charge |date=April 20, 2007 |work=ESPN.com}} were arrested early on April 20, 2007, and charged with felony possession of a weapon.{{cite news |url=http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/extras/celtics_blog/2007/04/telfair_arreste.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070422194656/http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/extras/celtics_blog/2007/04/telfair_arreste.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 22, 2007 | title = Telfair arrested |first=Greg |last=Lee |date=April 20, 2007 |newspaper=Boston.com}} The arrest was preceded by a traffic stop prompted when Telfair was spotted driving his 2006 Range Rover at {{convert|77|mph|km/h|abbr=on}} on the [[Bronx River Parkway]], a {{convert|45|mph|km/h|abbr=on}} zone. Telfair was driving with a suspended Florida license. Furthermore, when police searched Telfair's vehicle, they uncovered a loaded .45 caliber handgun under the passenger's seat. Both Telfair and Eden claimed to not have any knowledge of the firearm. The police were unable to determine the registration status of the handgun. In September 2008, Telfair pleaded guilty to criminal possession of a weapon and received three years' probation. In October 2008, the NBA handed him a three-game suspension following the guilty plea.{{cite news |title = NBA hands Telfair a three-game suspension |url = http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/30987449.html |date = October 15, 2008 |first = Jerry |last = Zgoda |newspaper = [[Star Tribune]] |access-date = November 2, 2008 |url-status = dead |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100128174622/http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/30987449.html |archive-date = January 28, 2010 }} On June 11, 2017, Telfair and another man were arrested on weapons and marijuana-related charges during a traffic stop in Brooklyn. Police pulled them over for driving without headlights on and illegally parking. Inside the vehicle, officers spotted a lit [[Joint (cannabis)|joint]], and a subsequent search yielded three loaded handguns, a semiautomatic rifle, a ballistics vest, and several bags of marijuana that were among suitcases, clothing, shoes, and furniture parts.{{Cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2017/06/11/ex-basketball-phenom-busted-with-car-filled-with-loaded-guns/|title = Ex-basketball phenom busted with car filled with loaded guns|date = June 12, 2017}} Sebastian was in New York at the time for what was supposed to have been only a matter of hours, being in between a move of residence, and for the opening of basketball courts at the [[Coney Island]] projects where he was raised. In April 2019, following a two-week trial, Telfair was found guilty of felonious weapons possession.{{Cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2019/04/25/sebastian-telfair-convicted-of-weapons-possession/|title = Sebastian Telfair convicted of weapons possession|date = April 25, 2019}} On August 12, 2019, he was sentenced to three and a half years in prison for the offense.{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2019/08/13/sebastian-telfair-once-hoops-phenom-sentenced-prison-gun-charge/|title=Sebastian Telfair, once a hoops phenom, sentenced to prison on gun charge|newspaper=Washington Post|language=en|access-date=2019-08-13}} His conviction was overturned by the [[New York Court of Appeals]] on November 21, 2023.{{cite court |litigants=People v. Telfair |vol=41 |reporter=N.Y.3d |opinion=107 |pinpoint= |court= |date=2023 |url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar_case?case=10437318633891493365&hl=en&as_sdt=6&as_vis=1&oi=scholarr |accessdate=September 5, 2024 |quote=}} Reported by ESPN from an October 7, 2021 indictment, eighteen former NBA players, including Telfair, [[Jamario Moon]], [[Glen Davis (basketball)|Glen Davis]], [[Tony Allen (basketball)|Tony Allen]] and [[Darius Miles]], were arrested on charges alleging they defrauded the league's health and welfare benefit plan out of about $4 million. According to the indictment, the former players engaged in a widespread scheme to defraud the plan by submitting false and fraudulent claims to get reimbursed for medical and dental expenses that were never actually incurred.{{cite web |title=Former NBA players charged in $4M health care fraud scheme |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32354861/former-nba-players-charged-4m-health-care-fraud-scheme |website=ESPN.com |date=October 7, 2021 |publisher=ESPN News Services |access-date=7 October 2021}}{{cite web | title=U.S. Attorney Announces Charges Against A Doctor, Dentist, And Former NBA Player For Defrauding The NBA Players' Health And Welfare Benefit Plan | date=April 27, 2022 | url=https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdny/pr/us-attorney-announces-charges-against-doctor-dentist-and-former-nba-player-defrauding | work=United States Department of Justice }} Telfair pleaded guilty to charges of fraud on March 16, 2023.{{cite news | last=Dolmetsch | first=Chris | title=Ex-NBA Player Telfair Pleads Guilty to Health Care Fraud Scheme | date=March 15, 2023 | url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-03-15/ex-nba-player-telfair-pleads-guilty-to-health-care-fraud-scheme?leadSource=uverify%20wall | work=Forbes }} He was sentenced to three years probation.{{cite news | last=Dolmetsch | first=Chris | title=Former NBA Player Telfair Avoids Prison for Health Care Fraud | date=January 26, 2024 | url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-01-26/former-nba-player-telfair-avoids-prison-for-health-care-fraud | work=Forbes }} He has been ordered to report to prison in August 2025 for six months for failure to abide by court-ordered community service and failure to report to the [[U.S. Probation and Pretrial Services System|U.S. Probation Office.]]{{cite news | last=McCann | first=Michael | title=Sebastian Telfair Gets Prison Time After Community Service No-Show | date=June 29, 2025 | url=https://www.sportico.com/law/analysis/2025/sebastian-telfair-health-care-fraud-1234858403/ | work=sportico.com }} ==Biographical coverage== {{See also|Through the Fire (2005 film)}} Telfair is the subject of the book, ''The Jump: Sebastian Telfair and the High-Stakes Business of High School Ball'' ({{ISBN|1594864470}}), by Ian O'Connor as well as a documentary film by Jonathan Hock, ''[[Through the Fire (2005 film)|Through the Fire]]''; the latter follows Telfair through his final year in high school and accounts his decision to choose the NBA over college. Telfair is the cousin of [[Stephon Marbury]], a former NBA and [[Chinese Basketball Association|CBA]] star, and the half-brother of former NBA player [[Jamel Thomas]]. Attending Lincoln High School in the Coney Island section of Brooklyn, Telfair was the school's all-time leading scorer until [[Lance Stephenson]] broke his record in 2009. Telfair was also named [[Mr. New York Basketball|New York State Mr. Basketball]] following his outstanding senior season at Lincoln.
